name: safe_cut
note: REVIEW: start value. An outfit whose picture-vector similarity to the user's taste vector (the mean of the wardrobe's FashionCLIP vectors, plus outfit feedback) is at least this is labelled 'safe'. Chosen on the frozen golden wardrobe (backend/tests/golden/wardrobe.json): the 12 completed outfits score 0.85-0.93 (33rd percentile 0.90), and the outfits the goldens show score 0.73-0.93. 0.892 sits in the biggest gap between two shown values (0.888 and 0.896), so the label does not flip on rounding.

name: bolder_cut
note: REVIEW: start value. From this similarity up to safe_cut the label is 'bolder'; below it, 'experimental'. 0.777 sits in the biggest gap between two shown values on the golden wardrobe (0.763 and 0.791), so the golden answers show all three labels (the man's golden wardrobe too: 0.94 safe, 0.87 bolder, 0.62 experimental for the swimsuit).

name: min_wardrobe_items
note: REVIEW: start value. With fewer usable pieces (after the modesty / season / occasion filters) than this, the outfits are shown with LOW confidence. Same start value as verdict_rules.csv, kept apart so each feature is tuned on its own.

name: wear_penalty_days
note: REVIEW: start value 0 = no penalty. A piece worn within the last this many days (today included, in Tunis time) loses wear_penalty_points when outfits are ranked. Both this and wear_penalty_points must be above 0 for the penalty to apply.

name: wear_penalty_points
note: REVIEW: start value 0 = no penalty. Points (0-100 scale, like the outfit score) taken off an outfit for each of its pieces worn within wear_penalty_days. The shown score never changes: only the order of the suggestions.

name: pick_pool
note: REVIEW: start value. The Dress page draws each outfit at random (from a seed: the same day gives the same outfits) among this many best candidates of its label. 1 = always the best one.
